description: From May to September 1909, Pablo Picasso produced landscapes, still lifes, and portraits—like this work—that are among the most highly acclaimed achievements of early Cubism. Here, by vigorously modeling the figure in a manner that blatantly disregards the rules of illusionistic painting, he shares visual information about the subject, like her bun, that would not be visible in a traditional frontal view.
title: Head of a Woman
